s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cutaneous eruption with hyperkeratotic papules
salient_findings: Reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the left leg
Slight bleeding after removal of scales
Compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 10-year history of slowly progressive cutaneous eruption
Eruption located on the front and back of the left leg
Papules are 1 to 10 mm wide
Patient has a 16-year history of diabetes mellitus
Diabetes is being treated with metformin
No history of another endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
No family history of similar cutaneous findings
Hematological and biochemical test results are unremarkable

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic papules and progressive cutaneous eruption match porokeratosis presentation

shortlist.label: Lichenoid keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and histological findings of hyperkeratosis and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with lichenoid keratosis

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic papules and absence of other systemic symptoms make psoriasis a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate and epidermal atrophy are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of hyperkeratotic papules and histological findings of bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with lichen planus

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly progressive, asymptomatic cutaneous eruption with reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules and the histopathological findings of compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate in the superficial dermis are consistent with porokeratosis.

rejected.label: Lichenoid keratosis
rejected.why: Lichenoid keratosis typically presents as a solitary lesion, whereas the patient has multiple papules on the left leg.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: Psoriasis usually has a more rapid onset and is associated with other symptoms such as itching and nail changes, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with more inflammatory lesions and scarring, which are not described in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus usually presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules and is often associated with mucosal involvement, which is not mentioned in the vignette.
